item.title: Re: SCP Concept: Reflection
item.content:encoded:
Once again, I thank you all for your feedbacks and I'll post this to you because I think you misunderstood the story a bit. Your whole understanding of this SCP is that it's main anomaly, the mirror, makes the individual's reflection possess the real one and make them commit suicide. This isn't really the case with my concept, my general idea and main focus of this is mostly the mirror because instead of it possessing the individual it manipulates them by turning the real individual into the reflection, thus making them follow the other's movement, so in general it just turns the person into the reflection sending them temporarily into a mirror dimension. They only die because by being the reflection itself if the mirror breaks the person dies with it and even tho the SCP kind of swaps places with the person it can't actually escape into the real world and will still be kept in the mirror. The gas station is simply a place where the main anomaly is stored, so that people who are on the road or passing by can take a quick break and go in there, which leads to their deaths.

(This will probably be the last reply I do so the posts aren't flooded with questions and answers)

item.title: Youtube Channels Inspiration List (Work In Progress)
item.content:encoded:
There are a great number of Youtube channels that produce content that can be really useful and inspirational when you work on SCPs and tales. I've collected quite a few myself over the years, so I thought it would be useful to make a list of Youtube channels that can help us write.

What I really want is contributions. I'm going to start the list, but I want to expand it as much as possible. I'm going to use a format that will make it as fast as possible for people to find what they're looking for. If you contribute, please use the following format:

1. Include a link to the channel (preferably the channel main page, not just a video from the channel).
2. The name of the channel.
3. The category that they channel fits in (see categories below, might add more as time goes).
4. Description of the content on the channel. Try to include a little bit about who might be interested in the channel. See below for a framework.

Also note: The channel has to be somewhat directly relevant to writing SCPs. SCPs focus on phenomena that deviate from the norm. The list shouldn't include channels that delve into more mundane topics, even if those topics might be relevant to a story. It might be useful to research how a diesel engine works if you're writing a SCP focused on that topic, but it's not going to be even remotely useful to most people who write SCPs.

Youtube Channels

General Writing / Storytelling

Just Write
Link
Just Write focuses on looking at popular works of fiction, primarily movies, and trying to decipher what good lessons can be learnt from the work to improve your own writing.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to use popular works of fiction as a foundation to improve their own writing.

Lessons from the Screenplay
Link
Lessons from the Screenplay, obviously, focuses on screenplays, often focusing each video on a single movie, going over the screenplay to explain what makes it so effective. Has a lot of videos that focus greatly on dialogue.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to cinema for tips on how to build tension and write beautiful dialogue.

SCP specific content

The Exploring Series
Link
To many on these forums, The Exploring Series was the gateway drug to the rest of the SCP community. Each video goes over a single SCP, telling the tale of the SCP in an interesting and captivating way, combining the story with images appropriate to it.
Who is this for? Everyone, but especially people who are yet not that familiar with the SCP foundation.

Real life - Investigation and policework

JCS - Criminal Psychology
Link
JSC focuses on the psychology of criminals, using interrogation videos as his primary source of information.
Who is this for? This channel is an invaluable asset if you want to create realistic interrogation scenes in your writing.

Real Life - Psychology

Dr. Todd Grande
Link
Dr. Todd Grande focuses on making psychological profiles of real-life murders and serial killers. Some of his profiles focus on other interesting people who are somehow outliers of society.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to create much more realistic and grounded characters, especially evil or malevolent characters.

Real Life - Philosophy

Academy of Ideas
Link
A channel that goes into great detail on some of the darker writers in philosophy and psychology. The channel explores archetypes, shadow projection, despair and similar topics.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to learn more about the darker philosophers like Carl Jung, Nietzsche and Kirkegaard.

Fiction - Horror

Acolytes of Horror
Link
Acolytes of Horror specializes in making fewer, but fairly long and in-depth analyses of horror. Primarily he analyses movies, but some of his videos focus on the historic influences on modern-day horror.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to really delve deep into the psychology and symbolism of effective horror.

The Vile Eye
Link
The Vile Eye makes psychological profiles of famous evil characters, from Nurse Ratchet in One Flew Over The Cuckoo's Nest, to Michael Meyers from Halloween.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to create a memorable evil character.

Ryan Hollinger
Link
Ryan Hollinger makes videos where he analyzes various horror movies, discussing what makes them effective.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to widen their background knowledge on horror movies.

Fiction - Thriller and Drama

Fiction - Science Fiction

Isaac Arthur
Link
This channel focuses on hard sci-fi topics such as Dyson Spheres and Matrioshka Brains as well as hypothesizes about aliens. A lot of the material might be a bit too large in scale to fit into the SCP universe.
Who is this for? Anyone who's interested in hard sci-fi and civilizations on a galactic scale.

John Michael Godier
Link
The creator of this channel is a science-fiction writer who focuses on hard sci-fi, with an emphasis on realism. The content describes a lot of hypothetical science fiction phenomena.
Who is this for? Anyone who's interested in hard sci-fi, especially concepts such as multiple universes and alien civilizations.

Like Stories of Old
Link
This channel is very philosophical, it goes into deep detail on topics such as time travel, the hero's journey, global pandemics and empathy. It can help create an emotional and philosophical underpinning to any story you tell.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to learn more about how sci-fi concepts and story tropes connect to a deeper philosophical and psychological truth.

Quinn's Ideas
Link
Quinn's Ideas focuses very heavily on the Dune universe, and as such goes into tremendous detail on topics such as psychic powers, genetics and omniscience. If you haven't read the Dune books, there are videos several hours long that go through each book. Has lately also started making videos on H.P. Lovecraft.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to learn more about the Dune universe without reading all of the books. Also a great source of inspiration if you're writing on omniscience and related psychic powers.

Audiobooks

HorrorBabble
Link
Has all of the H.P. Lovecraft books, as well as many other horror writers such as Robert Bloch

item.title: Re: prix0rs the Cactus
item.content:encoded:
Hello! I am here per our IRC exchange to offer crit

Crit lives within
Yeeted and Deleeted

ConProcs

The temperature in its containment chamber is to be kept at a minimum of 28 degrees Celsius.

I would indicate which direction this errs. Is higher okay? Or is lower?

This is an otherwise very brief section so I have little to say. We just get right on into it and I'm good with that.

+++Description

Two arms extend from the central portion of its body.

Consider: "Two arms extend from center mass"

via levitation, usually at most 0.3 meters above the ground.

Language cleanup and significant digits. Consider: "levitation at an elevation of approximately 30cm"

SCP-XXXX is sentient and capable of speech via telepathy.

You might mean sapient. You might also want to say "communication via telepathy" rather than speech.

recording a corrupted version of its speech.

"corrupted version" is highly dubious.

It is capable of firing regular revolver ammunition

Since we just switched to the -1 I think it's probably fine, but, you could maybe stand to clarify the noun here a bit better in this passage.

bullets with a trajectory unaffected by wind,

Wind is only a factor at distances which are pretty well in excess of the range of a revolver.

It then traveled 6 kilometers across the city of Hollister,

I want to bring this up because the entire rest of this article is just one massive masquerade breach and you never cover or refer to that explicitly. There are "sightings" and nobody seems to call out the fact a levitating cactus is talking to them as it fights crime. If you want people to be nonplussed that is certainly an approach you can take, but we, as the Foundation, categorically should not be abiding this as "business as usual".

Video Logs

SCP-XXXX 'kicks' open the front door to a Starbucks.

This factually can't happen so I don't get why we're being coy. The door explodes inward, or, the door opens unassisted. This isn't very clinical even though I know exactly what you mean.

evaded capture for approximately 8 hours

This kind of begs the question of escalation. Why are we letting some random embedded agents chase this guy for a full day without sending help? Reduce the number, or send help.

technicians who smelled gunpowder in the water supply

I don't follow what this is implying and it never seems to come up again. You also probably wouldn't "smell" gunpowder; it only has a distinct smell when it's been fired/spent and that's not going to happen in water.

I liked the characterization of the video logs overall but I do have to warn you about your dialogue; you use a truly stupendous amount of exclamation points, and when they are so common they lose their meaning. Please strongly reconsider how you are applying this punctuation with an aim toward toning it down.

The best place to use an exclamation is after an interjection or command word. This is a way to suddenly or notably raise the level of emotion so you want to apply it rarely so people notice the departure from baseline. If every other line has an exclamation then that is a very excited and exhausting new baseline. I can clarify further if you want.

I would like to read this again to offer more thoughts as you explore the issues with the town, or alternatively, tighten up the timeline so those issues can be brushed away. As it stands, I am having trouble getting into what you're presenting because of the issues with the framework. I will say, in general, the central character does convey a good sense of identity but I think that their perseverance in the face of a less accommodating world might make them come through even more.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: Re: Phantom Entry
item.content:encoded:
Oh my, thank you for the response!

So to begin with, this is not really like, an "anti meme" kind of "anti meme". It's a piece of entry in the database, perfectly readable, perfectly manipulatable, but the content DESCRIBES it as an anti meme, with the help of the entity claiming that it is. The actual entry itself isn't antimemetic, the content only CLAIMS that it is. This happens because documentation happens side by side with research, as requested by the entity because it is sating our curiosity to its amusement. Then after it departed, everyone involved instantly forgets everything and has each of their "unreadable" memory filled with vague fabrications, but the SCP entry remains, fully authorized and reviewed even. Hence, the "anomality" of the situation, where the containment procedure is supposed to be executed, none of the staff mentioned in the entry responded, resulting in disciplinary actions, but then turning into an immediate confusion fiesta where no one remembers about it, resulting in the proposal that the entry is anomalous.

Remember, this SCP is not really all just about the content of the anomalous entry, it's also about the validity of the entry, as it's at the end of the day just another documentation, only with no evidence. So this could be an anomaly in the system, maybe a security overlook and some rando messed with the database, possible sabotage, drunk researcher, who knows?

In the entry, the foundation really doesn't do much but interviews at first, since the entity creates the first impression of being another reluctant reality hopper, hence being treated as such. Standard Humanoid chamber, all that stuff. Each entry, the foundation catches it roaming more and more, sometimes suddenly in other SCP chambers, disappear from its own the room, interacting more and more to the point of making people uncomfortable and disturbed. Every time it does questionable things, it gets hit with another interview, and as the entry goes on this cycle will get deeper and deeper as it straight up appears in Keter facilities, roam outside of the protected area, "accidentally" causing a breach, speaks more aggressively, lose its charming attitude, etc etc. Basically, it's character changes questionably each passing day, and the foundation will be conflicted to take action as each misbehavioural instance caused no casualty, but is still dangerous until it goes so severe the foundation gets extremely desperate (where it gets a Keter label and is clearly uncontainable), and at the peak of mass panic, the entity settles down, reveals what it has been up to which is a research of its own, and went adios. There ends the entry.

But again, very important to note that this is an SCP entry about an SCP entry, which plays a huge part in the informational horror element, as viewers as left with a lot of doubt and questions regarding the entry. The actual, non-content entry will be very passive and boring because it really is just about a random documentation with no proof but is able to have so much authenticity in written permission, authorization, all the legal shenanigans. It basically will have weird pacing that kicks the readers in the end, saying "hey maybe all of that was lie lol".

item.title: Re: SCP: The Tooth Jar (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for your review. It's very informative.

Indeed, I omitted to present my ideas to build around this SCP, due to wanting to be very thorough with its description.

The article would describe the SCP in the usual objective fashion, complemented with tests to understand its properties :

For example, a log could feature uncomfortable D-classes eating through all sorts of food to test out which trigger teeth apparitions, and subsequently get diagnosed with some bone disease. Then, the article would show studies made about the transmutation, trying to understand exactly what kind of objects gets transmuted (do regular teeth also work?)

The article itself will describe the object's known properties thoroughly and the reader may make the rapprochement with the tooth fairy (but whether they do or do not is not very important).

I think this is enough to make a short article about a fun weird object that is at the same time somewhat cute (turning your fallen teeth into a small payment) and somewhat unsettling (teeth in your food, osteoporosis and radiations). What do you think?

item.title: Re: Night Terrors - Seeking Idea Critique
item.content:encoded:
I get like, the child manifesting horrors to protect herself from nightmares but my concern here is it feels weird to mix like…dream terrors with real protection? Like, why doesn't she create dream monsters that exist solely in her dreams to protect her? Obviously that wouldn't really be a SCP then but it feels…weird

I can see how that would feel weird! I should have been more specific but I was trying not to ramble on. I established that the child has C-PTSD, but I should have been more clear as to why.

I've loosely based the manifestation of her anomaly on "An American Haunting," if you've ever seen it. The narratives of the two children are quite different, but their situations are very similar. It's an incredibly heavy topic, and I want to make sure I write it respectfully.

The neglect by her mother, and unspeakable abuse by her father has caused the child to live her formative years in a near constant state of fear, and panic. Repeated physical, emotional, and sexual abuse she is unable to comprehend led to these frequent nightmares. After some time, her suffering was so intense that she began to lose herself in the nightmares, because they were less terrifying than her real life. Those nightmares then became a shield for her, and eventually a literal weapon.

Also if the monsters are protecting her, why are they hostile to all lifeforms (which might be a bit broad btw, like SCP-3749 shows, 'all lifeforms' includes 'bacteria' of which there are thousands in the air) and not just like, hostile lifeforms? Or even unknown lifeforms: it feels like if e.g. her mother approached, they wouldn't attack?

Oh wow, I hadn't even considered just how broad that could be. I suppose to be more specific I should condense it down to humanoid lifeforms and entities. Thank you for pointing that out!

As far as why it attacks all (decidedly humanoid) lifeforms, in my head she's been through so much struggle and pain at such a young age, especially by those who were meant to protect her, her brain perceives all beings other than herself a potential threat. While the child usually chooses flight mode, her monsters always choose fight.

So like, narratively what does this actually look like? My concern is that it feels like it could be very passive, but also like it might not be that interesting to read? It really depends on how this conflict plays out and stuff.

That is my biggest fear - that it wont be interesting to read. My idea was to narrate the process and discovery of her origin through incident reports, interview logs, addendums and such, while trying to make it concise enough to be reasonably palatable. My goal is make the readers feel sympathy for the child, while reasonably portraying The Foundation and the interactions between them.

Thank you so much for responding by the way! I appreciate it greatly.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlights: My Eyes are Up Here
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the clarification. Now that I'm clear on your intentions, I can offer a bit of crit.

+ Collapsing this as to save space
fwoop

I want to note that, in many ways, the subject matter is still uncomfortable. Even as I now understand your desire to make this an anti-harassment story, an anomaly based on the objectification of a woman's breasts is practically a minefield for things to go wrong.

I don't mean to say that you can't write this in a way that is respectful, it's just moreso to do with the subject matter itself. Sexual harassment, in general, is a dubious1 topic to write about. Once again, your intentions are essentially irrelevant if you can't articulate them in a way that gets them across clearly. (In this case, misinterpretation is a killer.)

Now, I'd like to touch on the actual story itself, setting aside my previous concerns for a moment. In particular, I'd like to get a bit more insight into the structure. I largely hold that the way you portray your narrative holds just as much, if not more importance than the narrative itself. (See also: the initial points in this posts. They link together quite well.)

From my understanding, there is an initial incident regarding Dr. Briggs that ends in his blindness. Following that, experimentation on Lopez. I understand that the initial incident serves the narrative purpose of introducing the anomaly while also giving the "pervert gets what he deserves" point, which is fine. I'm still largely unclear on the experiments, which really should serve some sort of narrative purpose. Are they going to make a nuanced point on anti-harassment? Or are they just going to serve as an explanation for how the anomaly works? I should note that the latter generally just… isn't interesting. A reader could care less about the inner semantics of an anomaly. An SCP article is a narrative that follows a specific format - if you end a story on "and THIS is how is all happened…", it's generally going to feel weak.

based on an interview with Lopez's parents, it is speculated that it might have first come about during puberty.

This seems to be another addition? Many of my points above apply here - what do you think this would add, would the reader really care about this? Would its inclusion benefit the article, or would it only serve as unnecessary bloat? As an aside, what do you hope to achieve with this point? Is it a subtle protest against the objectification of young women? It might be the lack of context, but the point as it stands is just… creepy.

Footnotes
1. I'm using this term very liberally.

item.title: Re: Anomalous Oil Replacement
item.content:encoded:
Adding on to the above, the Axis powers weren't the only ones developing technology at a breakneck speed during WWII.

The British, for instance, were heavily dependent vulnerable tanker shipments from the Middle East and the US for oil throughout the war, and The Petroleum Warfare Department was created both to help ensure the British oil supply and utilize the fact that they oddly never did seem to run out in the end. Operation Pluto in particular is an awesomely named project that in the real world involved building undersea pipelines from freshly liberated France to Britain in an absurdly short timeframe (as in < 1 month)- but maybe in the SCPverse that was just a cover for whatever they were using to conjure large quantities of high-octane fuel.

That also links to another interesting aspect here: one of the major factors in why the RAF kicked the Luftwaffe's ass starting at around the Battle of Britain comes down to the fuel each was using. In early 1940 the British introduced a new 100+ octane fuel and some complementary tweaks to their aircraft that had the Nazis scrambling to figure out how the British fighters seemed to have acquired a "+15% Engines" perk out of nowhere. The Axis's synthetic fuel program spent the rest of the war trying to play catchup against the Allies' seemingly magical ability to create increasingly high-octane fuel in quantities they could only dream of. In our reality it was the result of advances in catalytic processing that start with exactly the sort of quality crude oil that the Germans didn't have1, but again, in the SCPverse, who knows?

Footnotes
1. and the Allies starting to bomb the snot out of their existing fuel plants around that time didn't help matters any

item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Having the Axis use anomalies to fix a very real problem they had. Also I wanted to come up with a paratech article that wasn't just a weapon.

Okay but like…you understand the Axis are literal nazis right? Like they are the epitome of 'unsympathetic characters' which means you're going to have a really hard job getting someone to care about them coming up with paratech and a really hard job telling this story without glamourising the nazis because the way this is phrased implies they're gonna be the heroes here.

My advice is don't tell this story with the axis: find some other impetuous to have someone develop the tech (which isn't hard! there's been like four different oil crises! and even having an alternative that's less environmentally damaging could be a great like, economic opportunity or a sufficient motivation for a green organisation too!).

Beyond this: SCP articles are written from the perspective of the Foundation. If you want your article to be an interesting read, you're going to have to figure out where they fit in (and perhaps it's that they want the fuel source so they don't have to y'know, show up as a major purchaser of oil or handle loads of shell corporations to hide that).

TL;DR: if you have to put a disclaimer in your idea that you're not a nazi, it is perhaps worth considering whether the idea makes you look like a nazi unnecessarily and whether the idea glorifies the nazis.

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight: Tattooed hydraulic press
item.content:encoded:
I edited the greenlight a little bit

Seeking Greenlight: Yes
Page type: SCP Article

First of all sorry for my repost. I didn't get any greenlights or the amount of feedback I had hoped for. Also I'm new to the wiki so I don't know the proper channels.

The SCP is already written by me and is currently residing in my sandbox until I get enough greenlights to get the SCP reviewed.

Elevator pitch:
SCP-XXXX is a hydraulic press which from a first glance doesn’t seem that weird. It seems like just the ordinary hydraulic press located in different factories across the world. But upon further notice, you see that it contains several patches of skin with tattoos on them. To make things even weirder you notice that the skin doesn't match a specific skin tone (it differs from white to black skin tones). You come closer to the press and you're fascinated by the different tattoos displayed on its metalic frame. But then all the sudden…….

The machine transforms into a metalic cat like being with several blades coming from its body. The being moves closer at a fast speed and then all of the sudden one of its blades rips the tattooed flesh from your body with surgeon like skills. As you bleed your vision becomes blur. It gets blurrier and blurrier and just before you pass out, you see the being transform back into the hydraulic press. You see it pulvarize the flesh it took and then all the sudden your tattoo seems to appear on its metalic frame. Suddenly everything is dark and you're no more. But a part of you is now part of SCP-XXXX.

Central narrative:
A part of the SCP file is dedicated to the retrieval of SCP-XXXX. One of the researchers of SCP-XXXX interviews Agent Ford who helped to retrieve the SCP. During this interview we learn about the circumstances in which SCP-XXXX has been found and contained.
Example:
In 1988 several people went missing from a small town named Lockhart in Texas. A anonymous phone call from a women got the police to believe that the missing people were held at the Johnson & son factory in town. After some searching the officers and a foundation agent named Ford found a pile of dead bodies, their tattooed flesh ripped from their bodies. And next to it SCP-XXXX (the tattooed hydraulic press).

After the retrieval of SCP-XXXX the reader gets to read about research performed on SCP-XXXX. The reader learns about the nature of SCP-XXXX’s anomylous abilities. For example: SCP-XXXX has two modes of existence. It has its hydraulic press body which have several tattooed flesh patches on its frame, and it also has a secondary body, which is a cat like being into which the tattooed press transforms.

The research leads to several incidents and eventually to adjustments to the special containment procedures performed. While research is also starting to search for a way to use SCP-XXXX for the retrieval of other SCP's.
